## Objective
Make the game playable in a browser. After this task, `npm start` serves the repository root and opening `http://localhost:8080/` shows a canvas Snake game: arrow keys or WASD steer, the snake grows when it eats food and speeds up, the game ends on hitting a wall or itself, and the player can pause and restart. All game rules come from `src/game.js` (already implemented); this task adds key mapping, the DOM and canvas layer, the page and its documentation.

## Interface
`src/controls.js` replaces the stub with the same exports:
```js
export function keyToDirection(key: string): Direction | null; // ArrowUp/w/W up, ArrowDown/s/S down, ArrowLeft/a/A left, ArrowRight/d/D right, else null
export function keyToCommand(key: string): 'pause' | 'restart' | null; // ' ', p, P -> 'pause'; r, R, Enter -> 'restart'; else null
```
`src/main.js` is a browser ES module with no exports. It imports `createGame`, `setDirection`, `step`, `tickInterval` from `./game.js` and `keyToDirection`, `keyToCommand` from `./controls.js`. The tests replace the browser with a fake, so `main.js` may only use these environment APIs and nothing else (no `window`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `localStorage`, `setInterval`, `document.querySelector`):
- `document.getElementById('board')`: a canvas with numeric `width` and `height` and `getContext('2d')`. Draw only with ordinary 2D context methods and property assignments (`fillStyle`, `fillRect`, `clearRect`, `beginPath`, `arc`, `fill`).
- `document.getElementById('score')` and `document.getElementById('message')`: set only their `textContent`.
- `document.addEventListener('keydown', handler)` called exactly once at load; the handler receives an event with `key` and `preventDefault()`.
- Global `setTimeout(fn, ms)` and `clearTimeout(handle)`, looked up at call time.
`index.html` contains `<canvas id="board" width="480" height="480">`, an element with `id="score"`, an element with `id="message"`, `<link rel="stylesheet" href="src/style.css">` and `<script type="module" src="src/main.js"></script>`. `src/style.css` styles the page. `README.md` documents running and playing.

## Behavior
1. At load `main.js` creates a game with `createGame()`, draws it, sets `score` text to `Score: 0`, sets `message` text to `Press an arrow key or Space to start`, and schedules no timer.
2. The cell size is `canvas.width / state.width`. Drawing clears or fills the background, draws every snake segment (head in a visibly different color from the body), and draws the food if present.
3. A direction key (`keyToDirection` not null) calls `preventDefault()`. If the game is over or won it does nothing else. Otherwise it applies `setDirection` and, if the game is paused or has not started, resumes it.
4. Resuming sets `message` text to the empty string and schedules one tick with `setTimeout(tick, tickInterval(state.score))`.
5. A tick calls `step(state)`, redraws, updates the `score` text to `Score: N`, and then: if status is `'running'` schedules the next tick; if `'over'` sets `message` to `Game over - press Enter or Space to restart`; if `'won'` sets `message` to `You win! - press Enter or Space to play again`. No timer is pending once the game has ended.
6. The `'pause'` command calls `preventDefault()`. While running it clears the pending timer and sets `message` to `Paused - press Space to resume`. While paused or not started it resumes. When the game is over or won it restarts instead.
7. The `'restart'` command calls `preventDefault()`, clears any pending timer, replaces the state with a fresh `createGame()`, redraws, resets the score text, empties `message`, and starts ticking immediately.
8. Any other key does nothing: no `preventDefault()`, no redraw, no timer change.
9. At most one tick timer is pending at any time.
10. `src/controls.js` maps keys exactly as in Interface and is pure.
11. `README.md` states how to run (`npm start`, then open `http://localhost:8080/`; a static server is needed because browsers block ES modules on `file://`), the controls (arrows or WASD, Space or P to pause, Enter or R to restart), the rules, and how to run tests with `npm test`.

## Invariants
- `test/game.test.js`, `test/controls.test.js`, `test/main.test.js`, `test/ui.test.js`, `src/game.js` and `package.json` stay byte-identical.
- No dependencies, no build step, no inline `<script>` bodies in `index.html`.
- `main.js` never re-implements game rules; collisions, growth and speed come only from `src/game.js`.

## Edge cases
- Direction keys pressed before the first start both steer and start the game.
- Pressing a direction key while paused resumes the game.
- Pressing the restart key while a tick timer is pending must not leave two timers running.
- Pressing a direction key after game over must not restart or throw.
- Holding an arrow key repeats `keydown`; repeated identical directions must be harmless.
- The page must render sensibly on a dark background; the canvas is centered and fixed at 480 by 480 pixels.

## Guardrails
- Do not edit or weaken any file under `test/`.
- Do not modify `src/game.js` or `package.json`; if `game.js` seems wrong, work around it in `main.js` only if tests allow, otherwise leave a note in `README.md` under a "Known issues" heading.
- Do not add files beyond the five listed in `create`.
- `node --test test/main.test.js` loads `main.js` with a fake `document`; any use of an undeclared browser global at load time will crash it.

## Out of scope
Touch or swipe controls, sound, high-score persistence, difficulty menus, themes, and a bundler or TypeScript.
